frontMatter.introduction:
Welcome to the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual for BR Agrotech Limited.
This document serves as a comprehensive guide for our employees and stakeholders, detailing the standardized processes and procedures essential for the efficient, safe, and consistent operation of our agrochemical production processes.

At BR Agrotech, we are dedicated to maintaining the highest standards of quality, environmental safety, and operational efficiency across all functions of our organization. This SOP manual provides clear, structured, and practical instructions for executing various tasks within the company, ensuring our operations remain streamlined, consistent, and fully compliant with applicable industry regulations, environmental standards, and safety protocols.

The procedures outlined herein are vital for preserving the integrity, safety, and effectiveness of our products, as well as fostering trustworthy business relationships with our partners, clients, and communities. We expect all employees to understand, follow, and uphold these procedures to build a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and excellence.

Rooted in our mission to support sustainable agriculture, protect ecosystems, and promote ethical business conduct, this manual also serves as a framework for embedding responsible practices throughout every stage of our operations.

By doing so, BR Agrotech Limited reinforces its commitment to long-term agricultural innovation, environmental stewardship, and meaningful community impact.
frontMatter.scope: This SOP Manual applies to all operational areas of BR Agrotech Limited, including production, quality control, warehousing, administration, finance, employee management, health and safety, and environmental practices. It provides clear, standardized procedures to ensure efficiency, consistency, and compliance with all relevant regulatory and company requirements. The manual is applicable to all employees and stakeholders, serving as a reference for maintaining quality, safety, and ethical standards in the manufacturing of agrochemicals. Regular updates will be made to reflect changes in policies, regulations, and industry practices.
frontMatter.reviewMechanism: Regular updates will be made to reflect changes in policies, regulations, and industry practices.

blocks.text:
Objective:
We at BR Agrotech Limited are committed to sustainable energy practices throughout our agrochemical production operations. This SOP outlines procedures for optimizing energy consumption, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and enhancing operational efficiency across our manufacturing units. The focus remains on minimizing energy use, lowering carbon emissions, and ensuring full compliance with environmental regulations.

Scope:
This SOP applies to all operational functions within BR Agrotech Limited, including manufacturing, formulation, quality control, warehouse operations, and administrative areas. It covers all aspects of energy management, including energy procurement, usage monitoring, energy audits, efficiency improvements, renewable energy adoption, and carbon emissions reduction initiatives.

body.text: BR Agrotech Limited has implemented several targeted initiatives to enhance energy efficiency across its agrochemical manufacturing operations. These efforts are aligned with our commitment to reducing energy consumption, lowering operational costs, and minimizing environmental impact:

steps.heading: Installation of Compressors with Variable Frequency Drives (VFD)

body.text: To address the high energy demand of air compression, compressors equipped with Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) has been installed. VFDs enable precise control over motor speed by adjusting the frequency and voltage supplied to the motor based on real-time air demand, significantly reducing power consumption during periods of low load. The result is improved efficiency, reduced wear on equipment, and energy savings of up to 30% compared to fixed-speed systems. It is applied to all primary air compressor units and regular performance audits are scheduled to monitor energy savings and maintain efficiency.

In line with international energy performance standards, All major motor-driven systems have been upgraded from IE2 (High Efficiency) to IE3 (Premium Efficiency) class motors. The transition has been applied across key manufacturing equipment such as pumps, agitators, and ventilation systems. IE3 motors offer higher energy efficiency and lower operating temperatures, leading to enhanced durability and reduced energy loss. This transition supports long-term performance reliability while contributing to overall reductions in electricity usage across production units.

Conventional lighting fixtures have been replaced with energy-efficient LED lights throughout all operational areas, including manufacturing floors, storage zones, and administrative offices. These lighting options significantly reduce electricity consumption compared to conventional lighting systems. With their longer lifespan, they help to reduce maintenance costs and the need for frequent replacements, contributing to both operational savings and enhanced sustainability efforts. This upgrade supports B R Agrotech’s commitment to improving energy efficiency and reducing environmental impact across all facilities.

As part of its long-term sustainability commitments, BR Agrotech has undertaken a strategic transition toward cleaner-burning natural gas across several of its key operations. Recognizing the environmental and operational advantages of adopting a lower-carbon fuel, the company has shifted from diesel-fired air heating systems to natural gas-based systems for critical units such as the “Fluidized Bed Dryer” and “Spray Dryers”.

This shift has led to a significant reduction in greenhouse gas emissions and enhanced energy efficiency across the converted systems. The use of natural gas enhances combustion quality, reduces maintenance needs, and strengthens compliance with environmental regulations. BR Agrotech continues to assess and expand the transition wherever feasible, with the goal of minimizing its carbon footprint and supporting cleaner, more efficient production in the long term.

BR Agrotech’s formulation process has a design that operates without generation of excess or waste heat, thereby eliminating the need for any waste heat recovery systems. The production setup emphasizes ambient-condition processing, efficient mechanical design, and low-energy operations that inherently prevent the release of residual thermal energy.
Key features of the zero heat generation approach include:

Ambient Temperature Processing: All formulation activities—including blending, mixing, and homogenization—are conducted at room temperature or under minimal controlled conditions. This design ensures that no additional thermal energy is introduced into the system, effectively avoiding any waste heat buildup.
Energy-Efficient Equipment Design: Equipment such as agitators, mixers, and conveyors used in the formulation process are selected and calibrated for low-energy consumption and minimal friction. This significantly reduces incidental heat produced from mechanical operations.
No Combustion or High-Temperature Inputs: The process architecture avoids any use of high-temperature reactions, steam systems, or combustion-based heating. As a result, there are no hot exhausts or thermal discharges that would typically necessitate a heat recovery mechanism.
Thermal Equilibrium Maintenance: Process conditions are maintained in a thermally stable state, with temperature variations kept within tight tolerances. This ensures consistent product quality while also eliminating the generation of waste heat.

Daily energy monitoring is conducted across all departments using strategically installed energy meters. These meters provide accurate readings of energy consumption at the equipment and departmental level, enabling close tracking of usage patterns. By analyzing daily data, the operations team identifies areas with higher-than-expected energy use and implements corrective actions promptly to maintain efficiency.

This hands-on approach supports effective energy management in both production and administrative areas. Additionally, monitoring results are reviewed regularly to inform decisions related to equipment optimization, load balancing, and scheduling, thereby contributing to reduced energy waste and improved operational performance.
The following procedure has been defined that will be followed for the safe and efficient installation of a solar power plant at BR Agrotech.

Evaluate available space, sunlight exposure, shading, structural integrity, and load requirements. Ensure compliance with applicable regulations and utility standards.
Prepare panel layout, inverter capacity, cabling plan, and mounting structure specifications. Obtain internal approvals and required government or utility permits.
Source approved solar modules, inverters, cables, structures, and monitoring tools. Inspect all materials on delivery for quality and conformity.
Set up and align mounting structures securely. Install solar panels with appropriate spacing and ensure no shading or structural strain.
Connect modules to inverters and inverters to the LT panel using approved DC/AC cabling. Install earthing and lightning protection systems.
Mount inverters in shaded, ventilated areas. Configure monitoring software to track performance and detect faults.
Carry out electrical testing (insulation, polarity, continuity). Energize the system and verify performance. Document all test results.
Train the in-house team on system operations, safety measures, and fault reporting. Hand over user manuals, warranty cards, and maintenance schedules.
File net metering and regulatory documents. Record system details in the asset management system for future maintenance and audits.

BR Agrotech has adopted Post-Combustion Capture Technology to reduce CO₂ emissions from its manufacturing processes. Exhaust gases containing carbon dioxide are directed through amine-based absorption system, where CO₂ is effectively captured and separated from other gases. The captured CO₂ is then purified, compressed, and directed toward safe disposal or potential reuse, while the solvent used in the process is regenerated and recycled for continuous operation. The CCS system is supported by continuous monitoring and regular maintenance to ensure optimal efficiency and system reliability. Performance data is collected and reported to track CO2 capture rates and maintain compliance with environmental goals, helping BR Agrotech minimize its carbon footprint.

Carbon Footprint Calculation:

BR Agrotech undertakes comprehensive carbon footprint assessments to quantify and manage its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The calculation process follows internationally recognized standards, primarily the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol, ensuring consistency, accuracy, and global comparability. Emissions are systematically categorized into:

Scope 1 – Direct emissions from sources owned or controlled by the company, such as emissions from boilers, generators, and manufacturing equipment.
Scope 2 – Indirect emissions from the consumption of purchased electricity, steam, or other forms of imported energy used in production and administrative operations.
Scope 3 – Other indirect emissions that occur in the value chain, including emissions from upstream activities (e.g., raw material transportation, supplier emissions) and downstream activities (e.g., product distribution, waste disposal, and employee commuting).

To support this process, BR Agrotech maintains energy consumption data, production volumes, transport logs, and supplier information. These data points are used to calculate CO₂-equivalent emissions across all scopes. Regular third-party carbon audits are performed to monitor emissions trends over time, assess progress toward emission reduction targets, and identify opportunities for further energy efficiency or cleaner technologies. These audits also aid in maintaining regulatory compliance, improving environmental transparency, and guiding sustainability initiatives across operations.

By embedding carbon footprint calculations into its environmental management system, BR Agrotech strengthens its strategic approach to sustainability and reaffirms its commitment to mitigating climate change.

To systematically assess and enhance energy efficiency across all the operations regular energy audits are conducted, focusing on identifying conservation opportunities and improving system performance.

substeps.text: Planning and Preparation: The energy audit is scheduled annually, in coordination with an authorized third-party energy audit firm. Key energy systems and equipment, such as transformers, air compressors, chillers, pumps, motors, lighting, etc. are identified in advance for detailed evaluation. The operation and maintenance teams are notified about the schedule and their roles in supporting data sharing, equipment access, and on-ground coordination. Historical energy data, including electricity bills, operational logs, and equipment specifications, are compiled to establish baseline performance.

Data Collection and Measurement: Real-time parameters such as voltage, current, power factor, temperature, and load are measured using calibrated instruments. Energy consumption records are collected for a period of 12 months to analyze trends in demand, unit consumption, and billing charges. Details of equipment load, usage hours, operating efficiency, and power system layout are recorded across departments. Special focus is given to compressors, chillers, pumps, and motors, where potential inefficiencies or energy loss are commonly observed.

Performance Analysis: All measured and recorded data is analyzed to identify energy losses, low-efficiency equipment, and systems with potential for upgrades. Equipment such as air compressors, Chillers, pumps, motors and transformers are evaluated for loading efficiency and specific power consumption. Power quality assessments, such as harmonics analysis and power factor checks, are conducted to evaluate system stability and penalties.

Recommendation and Reporting: The audit findings are compiled into a detailed Energy Audit Report, which includes: Energy Conservation Measures (EnCon); Cost-benefit analysis; Estimated savings in kWh and ₹; Required investment and payback periods.

Implementation and Follow-up: All approved recommendations are scheduled for phased implementation. The plant team integrates energy-efficient solutions. Post-implementation monitoring is conducted to compare actual performance against projections. A summary of improvements is maintained for regulatory compliance and internal review.

body.text: BR Agrotech places a strong emphasis on educating its employees about the importance of energy efficiency and sustainability. Regular training programs and workshops are conducted to raise awareness and encourage employees to adopt energy-saving practices. Employees are also encouraged to report inefficiencies or suggest improvements in energy usage, which are reviewed and integrated into the company’s sustainability efforts.

The company is committed to continuous improvement in energy management. BR Agrotech regularly explores new energy-efficient technologies and process improvements to further reduce its environmental impact. Feedback from employees and energy audits helps identify new opportunities to optimize energy use and reduce carbon emissions. Innovations are tested and implemented in various production and support processes.

responsibilities: Leads all energy management efforts, audits, reporting, and compliance.
Ensure energy practices meet health, safety, and environmental norms.
Implements energy-saving procedures during manufacturing.
Maintains energy-related systems and ensures operational efficiency.
Provides strategic direction and allocates resources for upgrades and innovation.

blocks.text: The EHS department conducts a biennial review of this SOP to assess its effectiveness and identify opportunities for improvement. Feedback from audits and employee engagement activities is used to adjust strategies and ensure that the company is continuously improving its energy performance.

sops.title: Water Resource Management and Efficiency procedures

blocks.text: To ensure efficient use and sustainable management of water resources at BR Agrotech by promoting water recycling and reuse, adopting water-efficient technologies, implementing rainwater harvesting, assessing wastewater quality, and preventing groundwater contamination.

This SOP applies to all operational units, utility systems, and support functions within BR Agrotech that use water or generate wastewater. It covers practices and procedures related to water conservation, recycling and reuse, rainwater harvesting, cooling system efficiency, water quality assessment, and groundwater protection.

body.text: These practices are aimed at sustainably managing, replenishing, and protecting water resources within and around the facility by implementing following procedures:

substeps.text: Leak Identification and Corrective Action: Monthly visual inspections of water supply lines and bi-weekly checks for cooling systems are conducted.
Acoustic leak detection equipment and flow monitoring systems are utilized for identifying and locating leaks in water supply systems, ensuring timely repairs, and minimizing water loss.

Upon detecting a leak, the water supply is immediately shut off to prevent further damage. The situation is then evaluated by the maintenance team to determine the extent of the issue, followed by the performance of necessary repairs. After the repairs are completed, the area is monitored closely by the maintenance team to ensure no further leaks occur.
Rainwater Harvesting: Gutters and downpipes have been installed on designated roof areas to efficiently channel rainwater into storage tanks.
A first flush system is in place to divert initial runoff, ensuring only cleaner rainwater enters the storage tanks.
Harvested rainwater is stored in covered tanks and used for non-potable applications such as gardening and cooling processes.
Regular inspections and cleaning of the collection system, filters, and tanks are conducted by the maintenance team to maintain system efficiency.
Water levels and usage are continuously tracked, and data is recorded to measure water savings and system performance.

Groundwater Contamination Prevention: RCC flooring for the storage of hazardous chemicals storage and sand pits are implemented near the storage areas are constructed. These systems ensure that any accidental leaks or spills are contained within a defined perimeter, preventing any harmful substances from entering the ground.

Chemicals are securely stored in sealed drums, which are clearly labeled and placed in designated storage areas with proper containment measures. This storage method minimizes the risk of leaks or spills, thereby significantly reducing the potential for soil and groundwater contamination.

Regular training is conducted to ensure all employees are aware of safe handling procedures for chemicals and are equipped to follow the best practices in wastewater and environmental management, thereby reducing risks of groundwater contamination.

body.text: To systematically assess and improve water usage efficiency across operations, regular water audits are conducted, focusing on identifying conservation opportunities, reducing losses, and enhancing water management systems.

substeps.text: Water Audit Planning: The EHS Team, in coordination with the Maintenance and Operations teams, regularly conducts water audits by analysing historical consumption data and monitoring water meters installed at key usage points such as formulation areas, utility sections, and cleaning stations. Key parameters including water volume and flow rate to maintain accurate usage records.

Assessment & Identification of Inefficiencies: Collected data is reviewed to identify patterns of excessive usage, leakage points, or inefficient practices. Equipment and operational processes are assessed to detect areas where water-saving measures, such as high-efficiency washers or reuse of treated water can be implemented.

Reporting & Implementation of Improvements: A detailed report is prepared highlighting inefficiencies and recommended improvements, including process optimization, equipment upgrades, and recycling initiatives. Cost-benefit analyses guide decision-making, and responsible teams are assigned for implementation.

Continuous Monitoring & Compliance: Implemented water-saving strategies, such as leak repairs and process modifications, are continuously monitored for effectiveness. Regular audits ensure compliance with sustainability goals, and ongoing improvements are made to enhance water efficiency.

body.text: The Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) has been installed with the primary objective of enabling water recycling and reuse. The treated wastewater is reused in various non-potable applications such as gardening and flushing, significantly reducing the demand for freshwater and supporting the company’s water conservation and sustainability goals. For the effective operation and maintenance of the Sewage Treatment Plant (STP), following procedures have been established, ensuring that the treatment of domestic wastewater complies with regulatory standards and significantly reduces the impact on the environment.

substeps.text: Pre-Operation Inspections: Daily visual inspections are conducted by the operations, maintenance, and EHS teams to ensure equipment, chemical dosing systems, safety equipment, and control panels are in proper working condition.
The operations team checks the chemical levels and replenishes them as needed, while the safety officers verify the functionality of safety equipment, such as fire extinguishers and eyewash stations.
Routine Operations: Monitoring: Flow meters measure incoming sewage flow. Parameters like pH, TSS, temperature, and BOD are recorded to assess incoming load.
Chemical Dosing: Based on influent characteristics, dosing pumps adjust the chemical concentrations. All dosages and any modifications are logged by the operators.

Process Monitoring: STP units including aeration tanks, clarifiers, and sludge pumps are checked regularly. Aeration levels are adjusted, and sludge volume is managed to maintain treatment efficiency.

Non-Compliance Response: In case of non-compliance, the EHS department investigates the issue and implements corrective measures such as adjusting chemical dosing, altering operational parameters, conducting equipment maintenance, retraining personnel, and increasing monitoring frequency. Incidents are logged, and additional sampling is conducted to ensure return to compliance.
Routine Maintenance: The following maintenance schedule is followed to ensure optimal performance of critical equipment.

Emergency Procedures: If an equipment failure occurs, personnel immediately follow emergency shutdown procedures. The EHS department is notified to assess the situation and determine the required actions. The details are documented in the logbook, and corrective actions are taken to prevent recurrence.

Emergency Repairs: A stock of essential spare parts, such as pumps, valves, filters, and other components, is maintained to reduce downtime during repairs. A list of trusted vendors is available for procurement if necessary. Repairs are logged with specific details, such as the nature of the issue, corrective actions, and parts replaced.

body.text: Approximately 75% of the reject water generated from the Reverse Osmosis (RO) system—commonly referred to as RO reject or hard water—is reused within the facility. This reclaimed water is directed to amenity blocks for non-critical applications such as toilet flushing and cleaning purposes. By repurposing RO reject water, the facility significantly reduces freshwater consumption and enhances overall water efficiency.

An air-cooled chiller 28 TR has been installed to replace conventional water-based cooling systems, aiming to reduce water consumption and improve resource efficiency.
Traditional chillers require large volumes of water for heat exchange through cooling towers or evaporative processes, leading to significant water usage and losses.
The air-cooled chiller utilizes ambient air for heat rejection, eliminating the need for freshwater in the cooling process.
This system helps reduce the facility’s overall water footprint and avoids the need for water treatment, chemicals and infrastructure.
It supports the company’s sustainability goals by lowering water consumption, reducing operational costs, and minimizing environmental impact.
The chiller has been seamlessly integrated into existing operations and configured to respond efficiently under various load conditions.
Regular monitoring and maintenance are conducted to ensure optimal performance in terms of cooling efficiency, energy usage, and system reliability.
The adoption of this technology reflects a proactive approach toward environmental responsibility and sustainable resource management.

New employees are thoroughly trained on the SOPs, safety protocols, and emergency procedures. Regular refresher courses are conducted to ensure compliance with operational standards.

Conduct trainings, ensures safe handling of chemicals, and monitors environmental risks.
Performs inspections, repairs, and preventive maintenance of water systems and STP equipment.
Monitors daily water usage and STP performance; maintains logs and ensures process efficiency.

blocks.text: This SOP is reviewed biennially by the EHS Department to ensure its continued effectiveness and alignment with operational needs and regulatory requirements. The review includes evaluation of water consumption data, audit findings, STP performance records, and feedback from operations and maintenance teams. Any gaps or improvement areas identified are documented, and necessary revisions are proposed. The updated SOP is then submitted to senior management for review and approval before implementation.

sops.title: Air pollution control and emission monitoring

blocks.text:
Objective:
To implement proactive and effective measures for controlling, reducing, and monitoring atmospheric emissions, particulate matter, Odors, and noise from manufacturing activities at BR Agrotech Limited. This SOP aims to support environmental compliance, workplace safety, and community well-being across all operational units, particularly those involving agrochemical formulations.

This SOP applies to all emission-generating activities and equipment at BR Agrotech. It covers the operation and maintenance of air pollution control systems, monitoring of emissions such as PM, VOCs, SOx, and NOx, and compliance with regulatory standards to minimize environmental impact.

steps.heading: Monitoring and Emission Control of Atmospheric Pollutants

body.text: BR Agrotech Limited has implemented a multi-layered approach to manage and minimize emissions, ensuring compliance with environmental regulations and supporting sustainable manufacturing practices. A range of preventive measures have been adopted to reduce the release of air pollutants. Our emission control and monitoring framework encompasses the following key actions and technologies such as installation of high-efficiency dust collection systems, proper enclosure of emission sources, scheduling of high-emission operations during low-impact hours, and regular maintenance of pollution control equipment.
Installation of Emission Control Systems:
1. Particulate Matter Mitigation

A bag filter system with stack has been installed to capture particulate emissions from powder processing areas.
The stack is directly attached with the Pulse Jet Dust Collectors (PJDCs) of powder formulation blenders, Fluidized Bed Dryers (FBDs) drying chambers & spray dryer systems ensuring targeted extraction of airborne particulates during solid formulation operations.
Spot extractors are installed in high-dust generation areas, further enhancing the localized capture of airborne particulates directly at their source.
Closed-loop systems are implemented wherever possible to prevent the release of dust into the work environment.
Local exhaust ventilation systems are used during powder mixing and transfer processes to control fugitive emissions.
A regular cleaning schedule is maintained to avoid dust buildup in operational zones.
These combined measures have significantly controlled particulate matter emissions, ensuring compliance with environmental standards and safer workplace air quality.
1. Gaseous Emission Mitigation

A wet scrubber system has been installed to effectively reduce sulphur oxides (SOx) and nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions from process exhausts by scrubbing them with neutralizing agents.
A carbon tower has been deployed to adsorb Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) released during solvent handling and formulation processes.
The carbon tower is equipped with a stack attached directly to the carbon column, with a stack height of 9 meters, ensuring safe dispersion of the treated air into the atmosphere.
Both systems are integrated at emission points to treat exhaust gases at the source before atmospheric release.
Periodic maintenance, including carbon media replacement and system calibration, is conducted to maintain high operational efficiency.
These mitigation technologies have successfully controlled gaseous pollutants and help the facility remain compliant with applicable air quality norms.
1. Fugitive Emission Mitigation

A structured Leak Detection and Repair (LDAR) program has been implemented to effectively monitor and control fugitive emissions which cover critical equipment such as valves, pumps, compressors, and pipeline joints, which are prone to potential leaks.
To support continuous monitoring, a Natural Gas (NG) Detector has been installed, enabling early detection of gas leaks.
The detector provides real-time alerts, allowing for swift response and timely corrective action.
All detected leaks are systematically logged, categorized based on severity, and repaired within a clearly defined response timeline.
Preventive maintenance activities include regular inspections of gas-handling equipment to ensure operational integrity. The NG detector undergoes routine calibration and functional testing to maintain accurate and reliable performance. Additionally, comprehensive records are maintained for all inspections, leak events, corrective actions, and detector calibrations to ensure regulatory compliance and facilitate internal reviews.
Inspection and Maintenance:

A structured inspection and maintenance program ensures reliable operation of all emission control systems.
Critical equipment such as bag filters, scrubbers, carbon towers, and NG detectors are routinely checked for wear, blockages, and performance issues.
Filter replacements, carbon media changes, and scrubber checks are conducted at defined intervals to maintain efficiency.
Gas detectors are calibrated regularly to ensure accurate leak detection.
All maintenance activities, including inspections and corrective actions, are documented to support compliance and internal audits.
This proactive approach minimizes equipment failure and ensures consistent control of air emissions.
External Air Quality Analysis:

Quarterly air sample analysis is conducted by accredited external laboratories to verify compliance with local and national air quality regulations. These analyses cover key pollutants such as particulate matter, SOx, NOx, and VOCs, ensuring that emission levels remain within permissible limits.
The results are thoroughly reviewed by the EHS department accredited external laboratories. Any deviations or emerging trends are analyzed, and necessary corrective or preventive measures are initiated promptly.
All test reports, analytical data, and related documentation are maintained for audit readiness and continuous improvement of emission control strategies.
B. Vehicular Emission Control

Company vehicles undergo regular maintenance to ensure efficient fuel use and reduced Vehicular emissions such as VOCs, PM, CO, SOx, NOx emissions.
Regular emissions testing is performed on all vehicles, with non-compliant vehicles repaired or replaced.
Drivers are trained in fuel-efficient driving techniques to minimize air pollution.
All vehicles possess valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates.
C. Odor Mitigation
To control and mitigate odor emissions during QC processes, 1800 mm fume hoods have been installed in laboratory areas handling volatile or odorous substances. The following measures are in place:

Fume Hood Installation: QC labs are equipped with fume hoods that capture and extract odors at the source, preventing indoor or environmental release.
Localized Containment: All testing involving volatile compounds is conducted inside the hoods to maintain odor-free conditions.
Airflow Regulation: Hoods maintain proper face velocity to ensure effective containment.
Preventive Maintenance: Regular checks and maintenance of filters, exhaust fans, and ducts ensure optimal performance.
Performance Monitoring: Airflow indicators and sash functions are routinely monitored.
QC Chemist Training: Staff are trained in proper hood usage, sash height, and airflow safety practices.
D. Noise Mitigation and Preventive Maintenance

In agrochemical manufacturing, significant noise is generated by equipment such as formulation mixers, pulverisers, granulators, drying chambers, packaging lines, and ventilation systems. BR Agrotech has implemented the following procedures to minimize noise pollution and ensure the health and safety of its workforce:

Preventive Maintenance Measures: All equipment undergoes routine maintenance to maintain operation within regulated noise thresholds. A dedicated noise preventive maintenance plan ensures the early detection and rectification of noise-causing faults.
Noise Monitoring Program: Sound levels during both day and night operations are periodically monitored. The collected data is analyzed by the management for compliance and noise abatement planning.
Use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Employees working in designated high-noise areas are provided with certified ear protection, and its use is strictly enforced.
Complaint and Incident Handling: Any noise complaints or exceedances are logged, promptly investigated, and resolved by the Environmental Compliance Officer.
Equipment-Specific Noise Control Matrix: The table below outlines the targeted noise control maintenance plan for key machinery and the teams responsible for their implementation:

Ensure blade balance to avoid abnormal vibration

Maintain airflow efficiency for quieter operation

Ensure smooth mechanical operations to reduce noise

responsibilities: Ensures effective implementation and documentation of all emission, odor, and noise control measures.
Conducts inspections and maintains equipment to control emissions and noise.
Reviews air quality data and supports compliance with environmental standards.
Operate odor control systems and report any issues during lab activities.
Manages vehicle emissions compliance and driver awareness programs.
Follow safety protocols and report any emission or noise irregularities.

blocks.text: This SOP is reviewed biennially by the EHS Department with support from QA and Maintenance teams to assess effectiveness, ensure compliance, and incorporate findings from inspections and reports. Necessary updates are proposed to management and shared with relevant staff.

To establish safe and compliant procedures for labelling, storing, handling, and transporting hazardous agrochemical substances at BR Agrotech Ltd., ensuring the protection of employee health, safety, and the environment.

steps.heading: A. Unloading and Storage of Hazardous Substances

body.text: Unload Material: Hazardous substances are carefully unloaded by first verifying shipping documents and inspecting the unloading area for safety. Personnel wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), and a signal person is designated to coordinate movements. Proper manual handling techniques or mechanical aids, such as forklifts, are used for heavier loads while checking containers for damage and verifying received quantities. Once unloaded, the containers are transported to designated storage areas, maintaining cleanliness in the unloading zone. The shipping documents typically verified during the unloading of hazardous substances include:

Bill of Lading (BOL)
Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS)
Packing List
Hazardous Materials Declaration
Import/Export Permits

Verification: The quantity and type of hazardous substances are verified by cross-checking the bill of lading, Material Safety Data Sheets, and packing lists for accuracy, along with validating the Hazardous Materials Declaration and any required permits to ensure compliance with safety regulations, before moving them to designated storage areas.

Storage: Hazardous substances are stored in designated areas based on their specific classifications, ensuring that each container is clearly labelled with its contents and associated hazards. The storage area remains locked and secured to prevent unauthorized access, protecting personnel and maintaining safety protocols.

All hazardous substances are labelled in accordance with the Globally Harmonized System (GHS). Below given table provides a clear overview of the labelling requirements based on the Globally Harmonized System (GHS).

Indicates the level of hazard (Warning or Danger)
Describes the nature of the hazard
Provides measures to minimize or prevent adverse effects

Name, address, and phone number of the supplier
Instructions for safe storage of the substance

body.text:
Preparation and Training: Staff undergo regular training sessions on the properties of hazardous substances, understanding safety data sheets (SDS), and familiarization with first aid measures related to potential exposures.
Safe Handling Techniques: Employees utilize tools such as spill containment trays, tongs, and chemical transfer pumps, along with personal protective equipment (PPE) like gloves, goggles, and face shields to minimize direct contact with hazardous substances.
Spill Response: In the event of a spill, employees immediately execute spill response procedures, including evacuating the area and employing absorbent materials for containment and cleanup. All spills are promptly reported to a supervisor, and incidents are documented according to company reporting guidelines.
First aid kits and emergency response equipment including items such as:

Adhesive bandages
Antiseptic wipes
Gauze pads
Scissors
Tweezers
Burn cream
Eye wash solution
Chemical spill kits
Absorbent materials
Gloves
Face shields

Emergency contact information is readily accessible in all areas where hazardous substances are handled.
Employees are familiarized with emergency contacts and evacuation procedures specific to hazardous substance incidents, ensuring readiness for any potential emergencies.

All hazardous substances are securely packaged in compliance with applicable regulations to prevent leaks during transportation.
Packaging includes appropriate labelling that adheres to the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) for safe handling.
Containers specifically designed to contain hazardous substances are utilized to minimize the risk of spillage.
Vehicles used for transportation are equipped with necessary safety features, including secondary containment systems and spill kits.
Proper ventilation must be ensured within transport vehicles to handle hazardous materials safely.
Drivers receive specialized training on the handling and transport of hazardous substances.
Transport routes are pre-planned to avoid densely populated areas whenever possible.
Regular inspections of both packaging and vehicles are conducted to ensure integrity and compliance with safety standards.

blocks.text: All employees involved in the handling, storage, and transportation of hazardous substances must receive training on this procedure and the hazards associated with the materials they work with.

The procedure will be reviewed biennially by the EHS Manager to ensure compliance with updated laws and operational needs. Any incident involving hazardous substances will trigger an immediate review. Quarterly internal audits will assess compliance, while employee feedback will be considered during the review process. All changes will be documented, and updated procedures will be communicated to relevant staff, with retraining conducted as needed.

Effective waste management is a core component of BR Agrotech’s commitment to environmental responsibility and regulatory compliance. Robust systems have been successfully implemented to manage all types of waste generated from agrochemical formulation, packaging, cleaning, maintenance, and other operational activities.
Our waste management practices are designed to:

Waste Segregation to Prevent Contamination
Waste Storage, Handling, and Transportation
Promotion of Material Reuse and Recovery

Through a structured Waste Stream Mapping approach, BR Agrotech has identified and categorized the various types of waste generated throughout its operations. This mapping defines clear protocols for their segregation, storage, handling, and disposal in accordance with legal and sustainability standards. blocks.text: The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to define a structured waste management system that ensures the appropriate segregation, classification, storage, handling, transportation, and disposal of waste generated at BR Agrotech. This SOP is developed to reduce environmental impact, ensure full compliance with relevant environmental regulations, and support sustainability by encouraging material reuse and recovery.

This SOP applies to all waste generated during BR Agrotech’s agrochemical manufacturing operations, including formulation, packaging, maintenance, laboratory, and general facility activities. It covers all phases of waste management—from segregation and classification to storage, handling, transportation, disposal, and recycling.

rows.definition: Any waste that poses a significant risk to human health or the environment due to its toxic, corrosive, flammable, or reactive properties, such as chemical residues, expired agrochemicals, and solvent waste.
Waste does not pose substantial risks, such as packaging materials, or office-generated waste.
Waste materials like plastic drums, paper, cardboard, and metals that can be processed and reused through approved recycling facilities.
Biodegradable materials such as food scraps and plant-based waste that can be composted or processed in organic waste treatment facilities.

body.text:
Identification & Segregation of Waste Types

Waste generated across BR Agrotech’s manufacturing and operational areas is systematically classified and segregated at the source into designated, color-coded containers to avoid cross-contamination. All employees receive training to correctly identify and dispose of waste based on its type.

rows: Waste poses significant risks to health or the environment, such as agrochemicals, solvents, or residues.
Expired chemicals, agrochemical residues, contaminated PPE, used solvents, waste from formulation units
General waste with no significant health or environmental risk.
Paper, plastic packaging, food waste, sweep dust, office waste
Waste that can be recovered or reprocessed for reuse.
Empty HDPE drums, metal cans, cardboard boxes, shrink wrap, scrap metal
Canteen food waste, garden trimmings, biodegradable packaging

body.text:
Minimizing Cross-Contamination

- Separation of Hazardous Waste: Hazardous waste is segregated from non-hazardous and recyclable materials to prevent dangerous reactions or contamination.
- Dedicated Containers for Special Waste: Used agrochemical containers, expired products, and contaminated items are placed in sealed, leak-proof, and clearly labeled containers.
- Supervision and Monitoring: Supervisors regularly monitor waste segregation practices to ensure that employees are following the procedures and correct any deviations immediately.

Handling Special Waste Streams

- Expired or Off-Spec Agrochemicals: Collected and stored in approved hazardous waste containers pending authorized disposal.
- Used Packaging with Residue: Rinsed and handled as hazardous waste unless completely decontaminated; triple-rinsing protocols are followed where applicable.
- Electronic Waste (E-Waste): Faulty lab devices, batteries, and electronic components are collected and disposed of following the e-waste handling policy.

blocks.text:
Waste Records: Detailed records of waste generated, segregated, and disposed of are maintained. This includes:
Type and volume of waste generated.
Waste stream classification.
Any incidents of contamination and corrective actions taken.
Periodic Reporting: Reports are submitted to the Waste Management Team for review to ensure continued compliance with this SOP.
Routine Audits: The Waste Management Team conducts regular audits to verify proper segregation, monitor compliance, and identify areas for improvement.

In cases of improper segregation or contamination, immediate corrective actions are taken, including re-segregating the waste and retraining staff where necessary.
Root Cause Analysis: The root cause of improper segregation is investigated, and steps are taken to address the issue, such as refining waste separation protocols or improving employee training.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Employees handling hazardous waste wear appropriate PPE, including gloves, masks, and goggles, to prevent exposure to harmful materials.
Spill Management: In case of spills, employees follow the spill response protocol to minimize environmental impact and ensure proper cleanup.
Regulatory Compliance: Waste segregation practices align with environmental regulations, ensuring safe disposal and recycling of materials.

Review findings are documented, communicated, and audits are conducted to support ongoing improvement.

The purpose of this SOP is to streamline material management practices across all formulation and processing units at BR Agrotech, promoting operational efficiency and environmental responsibility. It provides clear guidelines to reduce material wastage, enhance resource utilization, and minimize the environmental impact associated with material storage, handling, and disposal. The SOP also aims to strengthen internal controls and promote the use of eco-friendly and safer material alternatives.

This SOP applies to all stages of material management within BR Agrotech’s agrochemical production lifecycle. It includes the procurement, inventory control, storage, safe handling, usage, and potential reintegration or recycling of raw materials. Key substances covered include active technical, solvents, dispersants, adjuvants, emulsifiers, and inert ingredients used in the formulation of EC (Emulsifiable Concentrate), SC (Suspension Concentrate), and other product types. The SOP also governs practices for monitoring material consumption, managing formulation waste, and embedding sustainable approaches in line with BR Agrotech’s environmental and safety objectives.

body.text:
Sustainable production at BR Agrotech emphasizes the use of environmentally responsible raw materials to reduce ecological impact and support long-term agricultural resilience.
Over 40% of raw materials used in packaging of product formulations are eco-friendly, including water-based solvents, biodegradable surfactants, and naturally derived carriers such as vegetable oil esters and plant-based adjuvants. These materials replace petroleum-derived and synthetic components wherever feasible.
These substitutions not only support sustainability goals but also ensure full compliance with international agrochemical regulations. Supplier selection is based on stringent environmental criteria, with preference given to partners demonstrating transparent green manufacturing practices.
Periodic material audits and R&D reviews are conducted to explore new opportunities for integrating greener inputs, further minimizing our carbon footprint and enhancing sustainability across the supply chain.

In line with safety and environmental goals, BR Agrotech systematically replaces hazardous substances with safer, less toxic alternatives in its formulations. This includes replacing high-risk chemicals with less harmful options that still meet performance standards. Mercury and mercury-based compounds, along with other severely hazardous substances such as chlorinated solvents and organotin compounds, are strictly prohibited and excluded from all production processes.
Safer input substitutes, including non-aromatic hydrocarbons (e.g., dearomatized aliphatic solvents), low-toxicity emulsifiers, and biodegradable antifoaming agents—are rigorously tested through internal quality protocols to ensure they meet BR Agrotech’s functional and efficacy standards without compromising product stability or shelf-life.
In order to opt for safer alternatives, no pesticides that have LD50 < 50 mg / Kg of body wight, which is falling under red category and considered extremely poisonous as per toxic categories defined in Insecticides Act are formulated.
Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) for all ingredients are routinely reviewed, updated, and centrally archived by the EHS (Environment, Health & Safety) team. Any substance flagged by REACH, GHS, or the Indian Insecticides Act for high toxicity, persistence, or bioaccumulation is reviewed for substitution during the annual chemical review cycle.
A structured monitoring framework, integrated with BR Agrotech’s quality assurance and EHS systems, tracks the performance, safety profile, and regulatory compliance of each adopted alternative. This mechanism ensures continuous improvement and supports our goal of maintaining a low-toxicity, regulation-compliant agrochemical manufacturing process.

steps.heading: Precision Dosing and Real-Time Process Optimization

body.text:
Material consumption is minimized using high precision automated filling machines. These machines ensure that filling of material is in the exact quantity required. This level of precision reduces material wastage.
Online monitoring systems are deployed across the formulation, mixing, and filling stages of production. These systems enable constant oversight of the manufacturing process, allowing for immediate adjustments to be made as necessary. This proactive monitoring ensures that material usage remains optimized throughout the production cycle and reduces inefficiencies caused by human error or process deviations.
Efficiency data collected from various stages of production, including formulation and packing, is continuously analyzed to identify potential areas for improvement.
The process ensures that resource consumption aligns with regulatory standards, improving both efficiency and compliance.

steps.heading: Reintegration of Residual Materials through Closed-Loop Recovery

body.text:
To further optimize material usage, BR Agrotech has implemented a closed-loop recovery system within its manufacturing processes. This system focuses on recovering residual materials from various stages of production, including cleaning processes, intermediate containers, and equipment flushes. Residual materials, such as excess herbicides, solvents, and other agrochemical ingredients, are carefully collected, filtered, and tested for quality assurance before being reintegrated into future production batches.
The closed-loop recovery system reduces the need for virgin raw materials, helping to lower material consumption by up to 20%. This approach minimizes environmental impact by reducing waste and conserving resources, contributing to a more sustainable manufacturing process.
The reuse of recovered materials not only lowers the environmental impact but also leads to significant cost reductions in production. By incorporating residuals back into production, BR Agrotech reduces the dependency on new raw materials, helping to minimize both operational costs and waste generation.
Ongoing assessments ensure that reintegrated materials meet the necessary quality standards required for product performance.

steps.heading: Reducing Hazardous By-Product Formation and Toxicity

body.text:
BR Agrotech has implemented advanced process controls and raw material substitutions to significantly limit the generation of hazardous by-products during agrochemical formulation. This includes minimizing volatile organic compounds (VOCs), heavy metals such as lead and cadmium, and Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) like dioxins, furans, and PCBs.
Reaction parameters are carefully optimized, including temperature control, catalyst selection, and mixing precision, to prevent unintentional formation of POPs during product synthesis and blending.
Engineering controls such as sealed transfer lines, and closed loop mixing systems are in place to contain emissions at the source and prevent release into air or water streams.
Chlorinated solvents have been completely phased out in favor of water-based dispersants and emulsifiers, eliminating a major category of hazardous substances from production lines.
Any hazardous waste generated is securely contained, treated, and disposed of through certified third-party facilities in compliance with Hazardous Waste Management Rules and aligned with international best practices.
The EHS team conducts regular audits, real-time emissions monitoring, and compliance checks to ensure the plant’s waste management practices contribute to overall toxicity reduction and environmental protection, in line with BR Agrotech’s commitment to sustainable agrochemical manufacturing.

steps.heading: Efficient Inventory Management and Material Tracking

body.text: At BR Agrotech, a robust inventory management system is in place to ensure optimal utilization of raw materials used in agrochemical manufacturing. Real-time tracking dashboards are designed to monitor the movement and consumption of inputs, enabling accurate forecasting, minimizing overstocking, and reducing material wastage. Just-in-time inventory practices have been adopted to align raw material supply with production schedules, ensuring efficiency across procurement, storage, and usage stages.

sops.title: Procedure for Confidential Data Handling and Breach Responses

blocks.text: Defines procedures for managing confidential information, including data breach responses and protecting third-party data from unauthorized access or disclosure.

body.text: Data Classification: Data must be classified into three categories:

rows: Highly sensitive data requiring strict access controls e.g., personal information, financial records
Data that is important to the organization but not classified as confidential e.g., employee information, operational procedures
Information meant for public consumption e.g., marketing materials, press releases.

body.text: Access Control:

Access rights are assigned based on the principle of least privilege. The Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP) refers to granting users only the access rights necessary to perform their job functions, minimizing the risk of unauthorized access or data breaches.
Roles and responsibilities are defined, and access is granted accordingly.
A quarterly review of access rights will be conducted by Data Protection Officer through automated access logs and reports, along with manual checks to ensure compliance with the established classifications. In case of non-compliance, access rights will be revoked, investigated, and corrective actions will be implemented, followed by a follow-up review to ensure compliance.

Confidential information is stored in secure environments e.g., locked file cabinets and secure servers such as cloud-based servers to guarantee encryption and regulatory compliance.
Transmission of confidential data is conducted via secure channels i.e. VPNs and encrypted emails.
All confidential data are encrypted both in transit and at rest, following industry-standard encryption protocols (e.g., AES-256).
Access to storage areas containing confidential data is restricted to authorized personnel.
Access control systems i.e. Lock & Keys are used to manage physical access.

Identification:

For IT Department

Regularly analyse system logs for unusual access patterns, failed login attempts, and other signs of data breaches. Logs provide a history of events, activities, and transactions across systems, applications, and network devices.

For Employee

Employees must monitor system logs for abnormal activities, alerting IT when suspicious patterns, such as failed logins or unauthorized access, are identified.

Employees must report any suspected data breaches immediately to their supervisor and the IT department.
An incident reporting form must be filled out and submitted to the IT department for documentation.
Depending on the severity, escalate incidents to management and legal counsel as necessary.

Containment:

The IT Security manager will immediately isolate affected systems to prevent further unauthorized access. This team is responsible for implementing containment measures, which may include disconnecting the affected systems from the network, disabling user accounts, or restricting access until a thorough investigation is conducted and the issue is resolved.

Investigation:

The Incident Response Team (IRT) will conduct a thorough investigation to determine the cause and impact of the breach. They will collect relevant logs and evidence, analyse data to identify vulnerabilities, and assess the breach's extent. Interviews with personnel may be conducted for additional insights. The team will document findings and prepare an incident report with recommendations for remediation. This approach helps prevent similar incidents in the future.

Communication:

Affected stakeholders will be notified via official email or in person, detailing the nature of the breach, affected data, and potential risks. Guidance will include recommended actions to protect their information, such as changing passwords and monitoring for suspicious activities. Regular updates will be provided as more information becomes available.

Internal Communication:

Management and the legal team are kept informed through scheduled progress updates, including regular emails being sent on their respective official email-ids, meetings, and incident reports. All critical developments, decisions, and actions are documented and communicated in a timely manner to ensure alignment and compliance throughout the process.

Remediation:

Corrective actions including revising data access controls, enhancing encryption protocols, updating security policies, providing targeted employee retraining, and improving incident detection systems are taken. These measures are designed to address vulnerabilities identified during the investigation and prevent similar breaches in the future.

Post-Incident Review:

A review meeting is conducted by the Incident Response Team, led by the IT Security Manager to analyse response effectiveness and identify improvements by enhancing communication protocols, refining the incident response process and upgrading security monitoring tools.

blocks.text:
Documentation Retention: Maintain detailed records of the incident, including timelines, actions taken, and any communications for at least three years.
Regular Review: The IT Security Officer, will review and update the procedures biennially or following significant incidents to ensure their effectiveness and alignment with evolving security threats and legal requirements

sops.title: Stakeholder Consent and Data Processing Retention and Disposal

blocks.text: To ensure that data is handled in compliance with stakeholder permissions, maintaining appropriate data retention periods and secure disposal practices to uphold privacy standards and regulatory requirements.

This SOP applies to all BR Agrotech departments and personnel handling stakeholder data. It covers the collection, processing, retention, and disposal of personal, financial, communication, and employment data, including obtaining consent, defining retention timelines, ensuring secure disposal, and maintaining compliance with data protection laws.

body.text: Consent is obtained through formal mechanisms through signed consent form and digital agreements. These documents clearly outline the purpose of data collection, how the data will be used, and stakeholders’ rights. Additionally, a confirmation process through email verification and electronic signature is used to ensure stakeholders have fully understood the terms before granting their consent.

Stakeholders are provided with clear information which is communicated through a Privacy Notice which outlines how data will be used, the retention periods, and the stakeholders’ rights regarding their data, including access, correction, or deletion. These documents are provided at the point of data collection, either in print or digital form.

Establishing Retention Timelines: Each type of data is categorized based on its sensitivity and relevance, with specific retention timelines defined according to legal requirements, business needs, or contractual obligations.

body.text: Tracking Retention Periods: Automated systems i.e. Microsoft SQL Server is utilized to track the retention period of stored data, ensuring that data is flagged for review or deletion once the retention period expires.

Secure Disposal: Once data is no longer required, it is securely deleted using methods appropriate to its sensitivity. For digital data, secure deletion methods such as data wiping or cryptographic erasure are used. For physical data, documents are shredded or incinerated in a controlled environment.
Compliance Checks: Regular audits are conducted to ensure that data is retained or disposed of in accordance with the established policies and legal requirements.

Regular Audits: The IT Department will conduct the audits of data access and handling practices. The audit will be conducted through a systematic review process, including examining access logs, evaluating data handling procedures, interviewing relevant personnel, and assessing compliance with established policies. Additionally, random sampling of data access and handling activities may be performed to ensure adherence to standards.
Continuous Monitoring: Automated monitoring tool i.e Intrusion Detection System (IDS) to detect unauthorized access and anomalies in data access patterns.

sops.title: Procedure for Employee Compliance and Awareness

blocks.text: To ensure that all employees at B R Agrotech are well-informed, understand, and comply with company policies, fostering a culture of accountability and awareness of relevant regulations and ethical standards.

body.text:
All employees must complete mandatory training on data protection, confidentiality, and security protocols during onboarding and annually thereafter.
Topics include company data protection policies and identifying security threats like phishing.

Employees are provided with updated handbook containing all relevant policies, which are reviewed regularly to reflect current laws and best practices.
Training covers immediate actions to report data breaches and the steps for containment.

Periodic campaigns reinforce the importance of data protection using newsletters, posters, and meetings.
Simulated phishing exercises assess employee awareness, with feedback provided for improvement.

A non-retaliatory environment encourages employees to report compliance concerns or suspicious activities.
Clear reporting channels, including the email id: hr.panoli@bharatgroup.co.in, are communicated to all employees.

Employee participation and training completion records are maintained.
Regular assessments evaluate the effectiveness of these programs, with modifications made based on feedback.

responsibilities: Complete mandatory training on data protection and compliance procedures.
Report any data breaches or compliance issues via the designated channels.
Ensure team members understand and follow the policies and procedures.
Regularly review compliance with training and reporting requirements.
Implement safeguards to protect data security.
Monitor systems for breaches and assist in root cause analysis.
Oversee policy implementation and enforce data protection standards.
Conduct audits and serve as the contact point for data protection issues.

narrative.text:
The IT Department conducts regular audits to monitor adherence and identify areas for improvement.
Participation in training is tracked by the IT Department, with annual completion required.

blocks.text: Non-compliance may lead to disciplinary actions as determined by the HR Department, including warnings, suspension, or termination depending on the severity.

The Governance Practices SOP is reviewed biennially by the DPO (Data Protection Officer) to ensure compliance with current laws.
Changes in regulations prompt emergency reviews, and revisions are communicated to all employees for acknowledgment.
